raw_title: 30 Lakh+ EVs Sold Under PM E-DRIVE, 8,610 Charging Stations Proposed
title: 30 Lakh+ EVs Sold Under PM E-DRIVE, 8,610 Charging Stations Proposed
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - PM E-DRIVE surpasses 30 lakh EV sales as government sanctions Rs. 904 crore for chargers and extends the Rs. 11,900 crore scheme until 2028 The PM E-DRIVE (Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement) scheme recorded more than 30 lakh electric vehicle sales by September 30, 2026, a figure presented at the recent SIAM National EV Charging Day. Government data had placed the tally at 26.59 lakh in June which means at least 3.41 lakh additional vehicles entered the scheme total in the next three months. The scheme began on October 1, 2024 and subsequently absorbed the electric two-wheeler and three-wheeler assistance originally available under EMPS-2024 from April that year. An August 2026 revision raised the sanctioned outlay from Rs. 10,900 crore to Rs. 11,900 crore and extended the programme until March 31, 2028. Importantly, the allocation finances more than purchase subsidies, as it also provides assistance for public transport, charging infrastructure and vehicle test facilities. Electric scooters and motorcycles have an incentive of Rs. 2,500 per kWh for eligible registrations from April 2025 – subject to a maximum of Rs. 5,000 per vehicle or 15 per cent of its ex-factory price. The ex-factory price must be no more than Rs. 1.5 lakh. The two-wheeler allocation has risen to Rs. 2,767 crore and the revised vehicle target stands at 45,79,120 units. Both privately owned and commercial registered vehicles can qualify if their batteries and approvals satisfy scheme conditions. The newly sanctioned infrastructure grants total Rs. 904 crore for 8,610 public charging stations proposed by states and oil marketing companies. The sanctioned amount represents 45.2 per cent of the Rs. 2,000 crore infrastructure budget. Earlier government records, dated September 28, identified Rs. 851 crore in approvals for 8,147 chargers. The subsequent announcement consequently indicates an increase in financial commitments but sanctioned installations are distinct from stations already operational. Eligibility for electric three-wheelers depends on their registration category. Registered e-rickshaws and e-carts retain assistance until March 2028 but the L5 three-wheeler incentive closed on December 26, 2025 after its target was achieved. Electric trucks and ambulances also receive dedicated funds, yet private electric passenger cars have no direct purchase incentive under PM E-DRIVE. State tax concessions and other programmes operate separately from this central subsidy. The purchase benefit is processed via an electronic voucher at the dealership. Aadhaar-based face authentication verifies customer identity, after which the approved amount can be deducted at purchase and the manufacturer can seek reimbursement from the Ministry of Heavy Industries. Vehicle makers must obtain the relevant technical certifications and satisfy the Phased Manufacturing Program requirements. Consequently, qualification depends on the approved vehicle and transaction, not merely on its electric powertrain. Public transport represents another substantial part of the programme. Authorities had allocated 14,000 electric buses by August 2026, of which 13,800 were assigned to Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Pune and Surat. The fleet procurement process differs from the retail subsidy for scooters and bus depots require considerably higher electrical capacity. The initiative also finances dedicated electric truck infrastructure and vehicle test facilities.

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Gaadiwaadi.com, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Cartoq.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - BYD India surpasses 20,000 customer deliveries as the Atto 3 and Sealion 7 secure over 14,000 handovers and the retail network reaches 40 cities BYD India has crossed 20,000 cumulative electric passenger car deliveries, twice the 10,000-unit total it announced in September 2025. The next 10,000 handovers took about 14 months, compared to almost four years for the first. The company presented its 20,000th vehicle to a customer at PPS BYD in Delhi on November 20, 2026. Importantly, the November figure represents cumulative customer deliveries since its entry into the passenger car market in 2021. The Atto 3 has contributed more than 9,000 deliveries, the largest disclosed model tally in the portfolio. The Sealion 7, which entered the market in February 2025, has already surpassed 5,000 customer handovers. Consequently, the two electric SUVs have together recorded more than 14,000 deliveries, a substantial portion of the company total. The Sealion 7 achieved its figure just 21 months after its introduction. The dealer network now consists of 51 showrooms in 40 cities, a notable development for a manufacturer whose first electric passenger model primarily served fleet operators. The company now caters to private customers as well, and its retail presence has grown alongside a more varied choice of vehicles. The current BYD portfolio comprises the Atto 3 and Sealion 7 SUVs, the Seal sedan and the eMAX 7 MPV. Model Body Style Technical Figure Basis Atto 3 Electric SUV Up to 521 km ARAI range Sealion 7 Electric SUV 0–100 kmph in 4.5 seconds Dual-motor AWD variant Seal Electric sedan Up to 650 km NEDC range eMax 7 Three-row electric MPV Up to 530 km NEDC range The original e6 introduced BYD passenger cars to India in 2021 and catered chiefly to commercial operators. Its successor, the eMAX 7, offers six- and seven-seat layouts, a distinctive alternative to the two SUVs and the Seal sedan. Meanwhile, the Seal provides a low-slung fastback body for customers who prefer a car to an SUV. The four models consequently address different passenger capacities and vehicle requirements. The electrical architecture provides another technical distinction between BYD and its established rivals. The proprietary Blade Battery employs a cell arrangement developed for durability and thermal safety. Cell-to-Body construction integrates battery components into the vehicle structure itself and can improve body rigidity and space efficiency. Separately, e-Platform 3.0 supplies the electrical and mechanical foundation for compatible BYD models and is designed specifically for electric propulsion. BYD has also entered the luxury vehicle category under the Denza name. The marque made its debut in November 2026 via the D9 electric MPV and Z9 GT grand tourer. The two cars occupy a different price category from the four established BYD passenger vehicles. Their introduction gives the company two distinct brands and a choice of vehicle types at the upper end of the electric car market. The manufacturer originally established operations in India in 2007 in the electric bus sector, well before its passenger vehicle debut. The current passenger car portfolio consists of imports, in contrast to locally manufactured alternatives. Separately, BYD has confirmed plans for the Seal U as its first plug-in hybrid in the country. The model combines a petrol engine and rechargeable battery, a departure from the battery-electric powertrains of the current BYD range.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Cartoq.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

raw_title: BYD’s Fang Cheng Bao Launches Ti 9 With Folding Steering Wheel
title: BYD's Fang Cheng Bao Launches Ti 9 With Folding Steering Wheel
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Fang Cheng Bao’s new flagship SUV could be launched in markets outside China as a Denza model sometime in 2027 Fang Cheng Bao, a premium brand from BYD, has launched a new SUV called Ti 9 in China. Denza does offer select Fang Cheng Bao models under its brand in markets outside China and could be planning the same for the Ti 9 sometime in 2027. Measuring 5,270 mm long, 1,999 mm wide, and 1,880 mm high, the Fang Cheng Bao Ti 9 is a full-size SUV. It has a 3,130 mm-long wheelbase. Like every other Fang Cheng Bao SUV model, the exterior is designed to project a tough, masculine image people associate with body-on-frame SUVs. The Ti 9 is based on a unibody platform, though. On the outside, the Fang Cheng Bao Ti 9 flaunts Brilliant Star Ring headlights, 22-inch forged alloy wheels with floating hub caps, Starry Sky door handles, and a split tailgate. Inside, the upright dashboard with vertical outboard AC vents, the high and wide centre console, and the boxy door armrests align with the authentic SUV character of the Ti 9. A 1.1-metre screen across the entire width of the windscreen mimics the Panoramic Vision system seen in BMWs. Also Read: BYD Yangwang U9 Xtreme Shatters 500 Kmph Top Speed Barrier; World’s First The highlight of the Fang Cheng Bao Ti 9’s interior is a folding steering wheel, which splits its rim into two sections and stows it in the dashboard when the vehicle is stationary. This helps free up space to, for example, add a tray table mounted via an accessory in the centre console. The driver can also use the extra space simply to rest more easily. All the configurations come with six seats positioned in a 2+2+2 layout. All six seats offer massage, ventilation, heating, and power adjustment functions. Under the hood, there’s a 1.5-litre turbocharged petrol engine that produces 115 kW (154 hp) and 225 Nm of torque. It is assisted by two electric motors, one at the front and one at the back. Both motors generate 200 kW (268 hp), but while the front unit develops 315 Nm of torque, the rear unit delivers 360 Nm. A 66.48 kWh LFP battery pack, which can be charged from 10% to 97% via BYD’s Flash Charger in just 9 minutes, powers these motors. Also Read: Kia Carens CNG & Clavis CNG Sales Get Past 6,200 Units Within 2 Months In India The Fang Cheng Bao Ti 9 accelerates from 0 to 100 km/h in 4.8 seconds and achieves a top speed of 200 km/h. It can travel 400 kilometres in EV mode, as per the China Light-Duty Vehicle Test Cycle (CLTC). The combined range of the plug-in hybrid full-size SUV is 1,630 kilometres. Prices start at CNY 2,79,900 (approx. Rs. 38.91 lakh) and go up to CNY 3,29,900 (approx. Rs. 45.86 lakh).

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Gaadiwaadi.com, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

The changes go beyond a new display, too. Bajaj has introduced an electronic throttle body, multiple ride modes and traction control, while also increasing the engine’s power output. The updated RS200 now produces 25.5 PS, up from the earlier 24.5 PS. It also gets a Sports Shifter, adding another layer to its riding experience. The motorcycle is priced at Rs 1,98,441 (ex-showroom, Delhi). The biggest mechanical change is the introduction of an Electronic Throttle Body (ETB). This enables multiple ride modes, allowing riders to adapt the motorcycle’s response to different riding conditions. Traction control has also been added to help manage wheel slip, particularly when grip levels are limited. The Sports Shifter is another addition to the package. Bajaj has not detailed its operating mechanism or whether it supports clutchless upshifts and downshifts, but its inclusion adds to the RS200’s updated equipment list. The cockpit gets a much-needed refresh with a new 5-inch TFT console replacing the earlier bonded colour LCD unit. The display supports Google Maps mirroring, bringing navigation information directly to the instrument cluster. The updated Pulsar RS200 now gets 37mm USD front forks, replacing the earlier telescopic setup, along with a wider 140/70-R17 radial rear tyre. article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Rushlane.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

article_paragraphs: The Indian automotive landscape continues its fierce rivalry in the compact and mid-size SUV segments as manufacturers battle for market dominance. Dispatches and field testing reports from Cartoq.com highlight pivotal updates regarding Indian Passenger Vehicle, bringing crucial technical, pricing, and real-world ownership data to prospective buyers.

Under real-world Indian driving conditions, certified ARAI fuel economy claims often diverge significantly from day-to-day driving numbers. While factory lab tests routinely claim 17 to 20 kmpl, bumper-to-bumper city traffic with active air conditioning typically yields between 10.5 and 13.2 kmpl for turbo-petrol powertrains, and 14.5 to 16.8 kmpl for refined diesel iterations. Highway cruising at steady speeds of 90 kmph allows these engines to settle into their peak thermal efficiency band.

Beyond raw horsepower and torque metrics, daily usability reveals subtle compromises that glossy dealership brochures rarely highlight. Rear-seat legroom, under-thigh seat cushion support for long family road trips, suspension dampening over sharp potholed roads, and actual boot space with a full-size spare wheel determine long-term owner satisfaction far more than high-tech dashboard gadgetry.

When evaluated against primary segment contenders—including the Tata Nexon, Mahindra Thar Roxx, Scorpio-N, Hyundai Creta, and Maruti Brezza—each platform offers distinct mechanical trade-offs. Ladder-frame SUVs deliver bulletproof rough-road durability at the expense of city ride suppleness, whereas monocoque crossovers excel in agile highway manners and effortless urban parking maneuverability.

Our definitive buyer guidance: identify your primary driving pattern before signing a booking form. If your monthly usage exceeds 1,500 kilometers with extensive highway travel, modern BS6.2-compliant diesels and strong hybrid powertrains offer unbeatable operating economics. For city commutes under 30 kilometers daily, a refined turbo-petrol or pure electric derivative delivers the smoothest driving experience.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Cartoq.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

article_paragraphs: The Indian automotive landscape continues its fierce rivalry in the compact and mid-size SUV segments as manufacturers battle for market dominance. Dispatches and field testing reports from Cartoq.com highlight pivotal updates regarding Indian Passenger Vehicle, bringing crucial technical, pricing, and real-world ownership data to prospective buyers.

Under real-world Indian driving conditions, certified ARAI fuel economy claims often diverge significantly from day-to-day driving numbers. While factory lab tests routinely claim 17 to 20 kmpl, bumper-to-bumper city traffic with active air conditioning typically yields between 10.5 and 13.2 kmpl for turbo-petrol powertrains, and 14.5 to 16.8 kmpl for refined diesel iterations. Highway cruising at steady speeds of 90 kmph allows these engines to settle into their peak thermal efficiency band.

Beyond raw horsepower and torque metrics, daily usability reveals subtle compromises that glossy dealership brochures rarely highlight. Rear-seat legroom, under-thigh seat cushion support for long family road trips, suspension dampening over sharp potholed roads, and actual boot space with a full-size spare wheel determine long-term owner satisfaction far more than high-tech dashboard gadgetry.

When evaluated against primary segment contenders—including the Tata Nexon, Mahindra Thar Roxx, Scorpio-N, Hyundai Creta, and Maruti Brezza—each platform offers distinct mechanical trade-offs. Ladder-frame SUVs deliver bulletproof rough-road durability at the expense of city ride suppleness, whereas monocoque crossovers excel in agile highway manners and effortless urban parking maneuverability.

Our definitive buyer guidance: identify your primary driving pattern before signing a booking form. If your monthly usage exceeds 1,500 kilometers with extensive highway travel, modern BS6.2-compliant diesels and strong hybrid powertrains offer unbeatable operating economics. For city commutes under 30 kilometers daily, a refined turbo-petrol or pure electric derivative delivers the smoothest driving experience.

raw_title: Volkswagen Tengo Compact SUV Production Begins, Derived From Tera
title: Volkswagen Tengo Compact SUV Production Begins, Derived From Tera
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Volkswagen Tengo enters production at Kariega after 2.6 million km of tests as the Tera-derived SUV will make its debut soon The Volkswagen Tengo underwent 2.646 million km of durability trials over 42 weeks before series production commenced at Kariega. The program involved 41 prototypes and subjected the compact SUV to varied road conditions where rough surfaces and inconsistent fuel quality required mechanical revisions. The locally assembled model derives from the Brazilian Tera and will reach South African dealerships in early 2027. Those trials prompted a sturdier rear axle, revised engine calibration for petrol of variable quality and separate exhaust, brake and fuel-tank components. Despite the mechanical changes, the Tengo retains considerable parts commonality: Volkswagen reports that 75 per cent of its part numbers correspond to Polo components. Consequently, the factory can assemble the SUV on the same production line as its established hatchbacks. Volkswagen has selected two petrol engines for the Tengo, a naturally aspirated four-cylinder and a smaller turbocharged three-cylinder. The 1.6 L engine offers both a five-speed manual and a torque-converter automatic, but the 1.0 L TSI is exclusively automatic. Both automatic versions receive six-speed Tiptronic gearboxes, a departure from the seven-speed DSG offered on other Volkswagen models such as the Polo and T-Cross. Volkswagen committed R4 billion to its Kariega operations in 2024, and the Tengo is the first SUV manufactured at the facility in its 75-year history. The new arrival also ends a 16-year gap since the Polo and Polo Vivo entered the production roster in 2010. Notably, about 45 per cent of the SUV components come from domestic suppliers. The plant will supply South Africa and export markets elsewhere on the continent. Despite the shared silhouette, the Tengo has its own front grille, bumpers, headlights and wheel arch mouldings. The roof comes from the Polo, but the functional roof rails and exterior mirrors derive from the Taigo. Even the wheel selection differs, as Volkswagen has designed three 16-inch alternatives and reserved 17-inch rims for the Style. The SUV measures 4.1 metres in length and occupies a position below the T-Cross in South Africa. The right-hand-drive cabin receives a revised dashboard, textured trim and a 10.1-inch touchscreen adapted from the Tera. Volkswagen has also specified a 25 W wireless phone charger, considerably above the 10 W unit in its Brazilian sibling. Higher grades gain digital instruments, a multifunction steering wheel and cloth/artificial-leather upholstery. The Trend and Life variants will arrive first, and the Style grade joins the range later. Safety equipment consists of six airbags, ABS and electronic stability control. Further equipment identified for selected variants comprises adaptive cruise control, autonomous emergency braking, front and rear parking sensors, a rear-view camera and hill start assistance. Volkswagen targets at least four stars in Global NCAP tests. The Tengo will compete against the Toyota Starlet Cross, Suzuki Fronx, Mahindra XUV 3XO and Chery Tiggo Cross in South Africa.

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Gaadiwaadi.com, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

raw_title: New Gen Hyundai Elantra Revealed – 157 PS Hybrid, Larger Cabin, More Tech
title: New Gen Hyundai Elantra Revealed - 157 PS Hybrid, Larger Cabin, More Tech
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Hyundai Elantra debuts for 2027 as an eighth generation sedan that gains a 157 PS hybrid powertrain, a roomier cabin and Pleos Connect technology The eighth generation Hyundai Elantra made its public debut at the ongoing Los Angeles Auto Show – three months after its introduction as the Avante in Korea. North American sales are scheduled for early 2027. The redesign is substantial: Hyundai has stretched the wheelbase, reshaped the body and introduced a different infotainment architecture, yet the car retains its compact-sedan identity. Inside, Hyundai has given the Elantra a 12.9-inch Pleos Connect touchscreen built on Android Automotive OS. The system supports over-the-air upgrades and third-party applications via the Pleos App Market, but its Gleo AI assistant can also interpret more complex conversational requests. Drivers can ask for destinations based on journey times and nearby parking, and the assistant takes those conditions into account. The 1.6 L hybrid delivers a combined 157 PS via a six-speed dual-clutch transmission. Alongside it, the new 2.0 L petrol develops 149 PS, or 26 PS more than the previous 1.6 L engine, and relies on an IVT automatic. Hyundai quotes 35 mpg for the petrol version. Powertrain Engine Output Transmission Hybrid 1.6 L petrol-electric 157 PS combined 6-speed DCT Petrol 2.0 L petrol 149 PS IVT The Hybrid Hierarchical Predictive Control System forecasts road conditions ahead and adjusts the balance between engine power and electrical assistance. Smart Regeneration System 3.0 separately recovers kinetic energy under deceleration, and Stay Mode operates climate control, audio and lights when the vehicle is parked. Consequently, those amenities do not require the petrol engine to idle throughout a stop. Hyundai has also revised the Elantra dimensions considerably. The sedan is now 85 mm longer and 30 mm wider, and its wheelbase has increased by 30 mm. Rear legroom measures 993 mm, a 29 mm improvement, and rear headroom rises 18 mm to 958 mm. Under the Art of Steel design theme, pronounced fenders and a long bonnet establish the proportions. Horizontal H-Edge daytime lamps contrast against vertical rear lights, and flush lift-up door handles accentuate the sides. The additional cabin space complements the furniture-inspired Curve of Upholstery design, which softens the otherwise angular character of the exterior. Importantly, Hyundai has retained physical switches for essential functions, and a narrow information screen sits in the natural driver sightline. Other equipment comprises two 15 W Qi 2.0 wireless charging pads, 100 W USB ports, Bang & Olufsen audio and Hyundai Digital Key 2. Six interior colour themes range from Black/Black to Burgundy/Rose Ivory and Chalk Beige. The safety provisions combine structural protection and electronic intervention. Ultra-high-strength steel reinforces critical body sections, and the available SmartSense suite has Forward Collision-Avoidance Assist 2, Blind-Spot Collision-Avoidance Assist and Safe Exit Warning. Lane Following Assist 2 and Memory Reversing Assist support lane control and low-speed manoeuvres respectively. An In-Cabin Monitoring Unit checks driver alertness and wheel contact, and camera-based occupant detection works alongside seat belt alerts and Rear Occupant Alert.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Cartoq.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

Its 2.0 L Honda Hybrid system is coupled to DualPower eAWD, and separate electric motors distribute traction between the front and rear axles. The SUV also becomes the first hybrid model to carry therevised Honda H emblem. Thailand, Japan and China are among its intended markets, and Australian deliveries are scheduled for April 2027. The Toyota Fortuner has a ladder-frame chassis, but the Avancier relies on a monocoque body and independent suspension. Honda has placed the hybrid battery beneath the second-row seats, nearer the centre of gravity. The new platform also serves future sedans and SUVs, and its body stiffness has been calibrated to preserve tyre contact under lateral load. Engineers adjust rigidity at individual structural points, and lighter aluminium components help reduce suspension mass. The cabin also benefits from the vehicle architecture. Honda has moved the gear selector to the steering column, which leaves more room around the centre console. Rear occupants receive large armrests, heated and ventilated second-row seats, and an extended panoramic glass roof. The door sills have also been shaped for easier access to the third row. Notably, the Australian RS has two individual seats in each row and consequently accommodates six occupants. The separate rear electric motor eliminates the need for a mechanical propeller shaft between the axles. Its controller distributes torque based on tyre loads, road grip and driver inputs, and it can react almost immediately to changes in traction. The system increases rear-axle assistance at a standstill and employs rear-wheel regenerative deceleration to limit forward pitch. Independently controlled traction intervention also responds to wheel slip at either axle. The hybrid engine works alongside a propulsion motor and a generator, an evolution of the established Honda two-motor petrol-electric architecture. The electric drive motor can propel the vehicle at low and higher speeds, and the petrol engine connects directly to the wheels at sustained highway speeds. Revised intake ports and piston crowns promote faster combustion. Honda has also improved lubrication and thermal management in the front drive unit to reduce mechanical friction. The 15-inch central touchscreen in the Australian version handles infotainment and numerous cabin functions, which also reduces dashboard switchgear. Separately, the 12-speaker Bose audio system supports Dolby Atmos and reproduces overhead sound channels in addition to front, rear and lateral audio. Voice commands can operate the climate controls. Honda also plans MyCabin remote functions that let owners check the parked SUV interior and its surroundings from a smartphone. Software updates will be available over the air. The exterior has narrow multifunction headlights, a substantial grille and a straight shoulder line that extends towards the rear. Flush door handles and a concealed rear wiper preserve the restrained profile, and the rear lamps have angular details near the wheel arches. The SUV also introduces the Motion Management System derived from Honda robotics research to coordinate power delivery and brake response. Honda plans 15 next-generation hybrid models globally by March 2030.

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Gaadiwaadi.com, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

Under real-world Indian driving conditions, certified ARAI fuel economy claims often diverge significantly from day-to-day driving numbers. While factory lab tests routinely claim 17 to 20 kmpl, bumper-to-bumper city traffic with active air conditioning typically yields between 10.5 and 13.2 kmpl for turbo-petrol powertrains, and 14.5 to 16.8 kmpl for refined diesel iterations. Highway cruising at steady speeds of 90 kmph allows these engines to settle into their peak thermal efficiency band.

Beyond raw horsepower and torque metrics, daily usability reveals subtle compromises that glossy dealership brochures rarely highlight. Rear-seat legroom, under-thigh seat cushion support for long family road trips, suspension dampening over sharp potholed roads, and actual boot space with a full-size spare wheel determine long-term owner satisfaction far more than high-tech dashboard gadgetry.

When evaluated against primary segment contenders—including the Tata Nexon, Mahindra Thar Roxx, Scorpio-N, Hyundai Creta, and Maruti Brezza—each platform offers distinct mechanical trade-offs. Ladder-frame SUVs deliver bulletproof rough-road durability at the expense of city ride suppleness, whereas monocoque crossovers excel in agile highway manners and effortless urban parking maneuverability.

Our definitive buyer guidance: identify your primary driving pattern before signing a booking form. If your monthly usage exceeds 1,500 kilometers with extensive highway travel, modern BS6.2-compliant diesels and strong hybrid powertrains offer unbeatable operating economics. For city commutes under 30 kilometers daily, a refined turbo-petrol or pure electric derivative delivers the smoothest driving experience.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Rushlane.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

raw_summary: Volkswagen has commenced full series production of the Tengo compact SUV at its manufacturing facility in Kariega, South Africa. The first unit is scheduled for a customer in Africa. Launch in South Africa is expected to happen in early 2027. Tengo is part of Volkswagen’s strategy to develop new market-specific models with the potential to generate high sales volumes. A sub-4-meter Volkswagen SUV has been confirmed for India as well, arriving in 2027. Volkswagen Tengo shares its MQB-A0 platform with the Tera compact SUV sold in Brazil. Around 75% of Tengo’s components are shared with existing MQB-A0-based models such as the Tera. In India, Skoda-Volkswagen use the localized MQB-A0-IN platform, which can be seen with the Kylaq SUV. The Brazilian Tera, African Tengo and Skoda Kylaq are essentially three regional derivatives of a single joint emerging-market compact SUV program.

title: Kia Carens CNG & Clavis CNG Sales Get Past 6,200 Units Within 2 Months In India
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Kia Carens CNG and Carens Clavis CNG record over 6,200 wholesale units since September as they have been well received by customers Kia recorded more than 6,200 wholesale units for the Carens CNG and Carens Clavis CNG in the first two months after their September 2026 introduction. The figure, announced on November 19, represents combined dispatches to dealerships for the two three-row MPVs. Importantly, the total measures vehicles supplied to dealers, not registrations or final customer deliveries. The Carens CNG costs Rs. 12.12 lakh (ex-showroom), and the Carens Clavis CNG starts at Rs. 12.39 lakh. The Rs. 27,000 difference separates their base prices, but the trim choices differ as well. Kia offers the regular Carens solely in Premium (O) CNG specification. The Clavis, by contrast, provides two choices, HTE and HTE (O), at the lower end of its variant roster. Kia also offers an ownership incentive under its Assured Buyback Programme. Eligible Carens CNG and Carens Clavis CNG customers can obtain an assured residual value of up to 75 per cent after three years. The maximum amount depends on the applicable mileage limits and other contractual conditions. Model CNG Variants Ex-Showroom Price Powertrain Kia Carens CNG Premium (O) Rs. 12.12 lakh G1.5 6MT Kia Carens Clavis CNG HTE, HTE (O) From Rs. 12.39 lakh G1.5 6MT The G1.5 petrol engine serves as the mechanical basis for both CNG derivatives, and a six-speed manual gearbox is standard. Kia has recalibrated the engine for the alternative fuel and revised the suspension to accommodate the factory-installed gas system. Each MPV carries a 60-litre CNG cylinder, and these changes distinguish the dual-fuel models from their petrol counterparts. The modifications also reach the dashboard. The driver can switch between petrol and CNG via a dedicated control, and the 4.2-inch colour TFT multi-information display provides a CNG distance-to-empty readout. The dedicated instrumentation helps motorists assess the available gas range when planning their next fuel stop. The rear cabin has received attention as well. Kia revised the third-row seat-back frame on both CNG models to improve the recline angle, a change intended to benefit occupants of the rearmost seats. Separately, the wider Carens Clavis family offers six- and seven-seat layouts, and its one-touch second-row tumble mechanism provides easier access to the third row. The Carens Clavis portfolio also has petrol, turbo-petrol and diesel versions. At higher trim levels, the MPV offers two 12.25-inch screens in a 26.62-inch panoramic arrangement, an Infotainment/Temperature Control Swap Switch, a dual-pane sunroof, ventilated front seats, a four-way powered driver seat and Bose eight-speaker audio. Selected variants have a 360-degree camera, Blind View Monitor and a Level 2 ADAS suite of 20 functions. Six airbags are standard in the Clavis family.

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Gaadiwaadi.com, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Cartoq.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

title: BMW R 12 G/S Launched In India At Rs. 25.40 Lakh
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - BMW R 12 G/S debuts in Pro trim In India as the 1,170 cc boxer twin, long suspension travel and off-road equipment are some of the highlights of the enduro BMW Motorrad has priced the R 12 G/S at Rs. 25.40 lakh (ex-showroom) and deliveries have already commenced at authorised dealerships. The motorcycle arrives solely in Pro trim as a completely built-up unit. More significantly, the local version receives the Enduro and Comfort kits as standard, equipment that customers in certain overseas markets select separately. The Enduro kit contributes an 18-inch rear cross-spoke wheel, off-road tyres and footrests intended for better control on loose terrain. Its 20 mm handlebar risers suit an upright posture mainly when the rider stands on the footrests. Protection comes from an engine guard and hand guards and a longer side stand matches the revised chassis dimensions. BMW moved the steering pivot forward and upward relative to other R 12 motorcycles and the tubular-steel rear structure bolts to a bridge-type main frame. Both suspension units are fully adjustable as the front has upside-down forks and the rear relies on a Paralever assembly. The saddle stands 875 mm above the ground and the road-ready mass is 229 kg. The wheelbase measures 1,580 mm. Component Front Rear Specification Wheels 21-inch 18-inch Cross-spoke rims Suspension 45 mm USD fork Paralever monoshock Fully adjustable Suspension Travel 210 mm 200 mm Enduro geometry Disc Brakes Twin 310 mm Single 265 mm ABS Pro The 1,170 cc air- and oil-cooled boxer twin develops 109 hp at 7,000 rpm and 115 Nm at 6,500 rpm. The horizontally opposed cylinders retain the classic boxer layout and a six-speed gearbox transfers output to the rear wheel via a shaft final drive. The engine has a 101 mm bore and a 73 mm stroke and the left-hand exhaust terminates in a raised silencer. Electronic assistance appeals to both road and trail journeys. Rain and Road ride modes suit paved surfaces while the Enduro and Enduro Pro provide separate calibrations for dirt tracks. Dynamic Traction Control can be disabled completely off-road and engine drag torque control separately addresses rear-wheel instability under deceleration. The partially integral ABS Pro also accounts for lean angle in corners and its front brake lever can actuate the front and rear brakes together. Despite its modern electronics, the motorcycle visually recalls the BMW R 80 G/S of 1980. The raised front mudguard, exposed engine and compact fairing follow the proportions of the original road-and-trail machine. The Light White paint, red saddle and period-style decals echo its historic colour scheme. Yet the X-pattern LED headlamp, centrally positioned round instrument and 12 V power outlet reveal the techn beneath the familiar design. Furthermore, two rear attachment loops can secure luggage. The Comfort kit provides Shift Assistant Pro, cruise control, heated grips, Hill Start Control and an adaptive headlamp. Its quickshifter permits clutch-free gear changes in either direction. Separately, BMW provides a three-year, unlimited-kilometre warranty and optional extensions can stretch protection into years four and five.

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Gaadiwaadi.com, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Cartoq.com, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

raw_summary: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways ( MoRTH ) has amended Rule 115 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, to revise the validity periods of Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificates. The Central Motor Vehicles (Sixteenth Amendment) Rules, 2026, were notified on 13 November 2026 through G.S.R. 991(E). Under the amended rules, PUC certificate validity will depend on the vehicle’s emission standard, category and age. BS-I, BS-II and BS-III vehicles will receive certificates valid for three months. Vehicles complying with BS-IV emission standards will have a validity period of six months.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Rushlane.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

article_paragraphs: The Indian automotive landscape continues its fierce rivalry in the compact and mid-size SUV segments as manufacturers battle for market dominance. Dispatches and field testing reports from Cartoq.com highlight pivotal updates regarding Indian Passenger Vehicle, bringing crucial technical, pricing, and real-world ownership data to prospective buyers.

Under real-world Indian driving conditions, certified ARAI fuel economy claims often diverge significantly from day-to-day driving numbers. While factory lab tests routinely claim 17 to 20 kmpl, bumper-to-bumper city traffic with active air conditioning typically yields between 10.5 and 13.2 kmpl for turbo-petrol powertrains, and 14.5 to 16.8 kmpl for refined diesel iterations. Highway cruising at steady speeds of 90 kmph allows these engines to settle into their peak thermal efficiency band.

Beyond raw horsepower and torque metrics, daily usability reveals subtle compromises that glossy dealership brochures rarely highlight. Rear-seat legroom, under-thigh seat cushion support for long family road trips, suspension dampening over sharp potholed roads, and actual boot space with a full-size spare wheel determine long-term owner satisfaction far more than high-tech dashboard gadgetry.

When evaluated against primary segment contenders—including the Tata Nexon, Mahindra Thar Roxx, Scorpio-N, Hyundai Creta, and Maruti Brezza—each platform offers distinct mechanical trade-offs. Ladder-frame SUVs deliver bulletproof rough-road durability at the expense of city ride suppleness, whereas monocoque crossovers excel in agile highway manners and effortless urban parking maneuverability.

Our definitive buyer guidance: identify your primary driving pattern before signing a booking form. If your monthly usage exceeds 1,500 kilometers with extensive highway travel, modern BS6.2-compliant diesels and strong hybrid powertrains offer unbeatable operating economics. For city commutes under 30 kilometers daily, a refined turbo-petrol or pure electric derivative delivers the smoothest driving experience.

title: Toyota Sales Breakup Oct 2026 - Hyryder, Hycross, Crysta, Fortuner, Glanza
raw_summary: Toyota recorded sales of 29,521 units in October 2026, down 26.67% from 40,257 units a year earlier. Compared with September’s 25,027 units, sales recovered 17.96%, adding 4,494 units MoM. Hyryder remained Toyota’s bestselling model, followed by the Innova Hycross and Innova Crysta. The year-on-year decline was concentrated in the Glanza, Hyryder and Hycross, while Toyota’s overall decline was 10,736 units. Gains for the Crysta and Fortuner helped offset part of that reduction. Toyota Hyryder led the lineup with 7,797 units, accounting for 26.41% of October sales. Volumes fell 32.52% from 11,555 units a year earlier, a reduction of 3,758 units. Sales rose 9.59% from September’s 7,115 units, adding 682 units month on month. Innova Hycross ranked second with 5,364 units and an 18.17% share. Sales declined 28.08% from 7,458 units in October 2025 but increased 16.74% from 4,595 units in September. Toyota will launch the updated Hycross on 25th November.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Rushlane.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle safety consciousness among Indian automobile buyers has reached unprecedented heights, driven by transparent crash test evaluations under the Bharat New Car Assessment Programme (Bharat NCAP). Verified technical telemetry reported by Cartoq.com provides a detailed examination of structural crashworthiness and passenger protection ratings for Indian Passenger Vehicle.

Under Bharat NCAP protocols, vehicles undergo rigorous offset frontal crash tests at 64 kmph, side mobile deformable barrier impacts at 50 kmph, and stringent pole side-impact evaluations. To secure a coveted 5-star safety rating, a vehicle must achieve high numerical scores in Adult Occupant Protection (AOP) and Child Occupant Protection (COP), while critically demonstrating that the passenger bodyshell remains 'Stable and capable of withstanding further loadings'.

What separates truly crash-resilient vehicles from mere marketing claims is the extensive deployment of advanced high-strength steel (AHSS) and ultra-high-strength hot-stamped steel along the A-pillars, B-pillars, and door sills. Standard fitment of 6 airbags, Electronic Stability Control (ESC), ISOFIX child seat anchorages, and 3-point seatbelts with pre-tensioners across all seating positions has now become the fundamental benchmark for modern Indian buyers.

In real-world highway collisions, vehicles with unstable cabin architectures risk severe footwell intrusion, steering column collapse, and door jamming that traps occupants inside. Indian carmakers like Tata Motors and Mahindra & Mahindra have raised the bar by engineering 5-star crash resilience into their entry and mid-size platforms, compelling global competitors to rapidly upgrade their structural standards.

Our consumer verdict: never compromise on core structural integrity for cosmetic add-ons like ambient lighting or fancy touchscreens. Prioritize vehicles with certified 5-star Bharat NCAP or Global NCAP ratings, verified stable bodyshell integrity, and standard Electronic Stability Program (ESP) to ensure maximum survivability on unpredictable Indian roads.

Greater ground clearance and larger underseat compartments are among the changes under consideration. The company could also alter battery configurations and electric motor outputs before production. All three Vietnamese models have hub-mounted motors but their distinct designs serve different requirements. The Evo-derived version is expected to have the lowest price of the three. Its Vietnamese configuration has a 1.5 kWh LFP battery and an optional second unit of the same capacity. A front disc brake, LCD console and 12-inch wheels are part of the equipment list. Its boot offers 12 litres of space when both batteries are fitted. The scooter also provides ride statistics and vehicle location information via a mobile application. Its 14-inch wheels sit beneath a family scooter body and a TFT console replaces the basic LCD display. Keyless access and hill-hold assistance are standard on the model as well while its underseat compartment measures 21 litres. The dual-battery arrangement takes four hours and 30 minutes for a full recharge. The Kinet has a sportier exterior and a different motor calibration. It can accelerate from 0 to 50 kmph in less than six seconds in Vietnamese specification. The scooter has a 22-litre underseat compartment and its TFT panel accompanies keyless access. Its battery refill takes nine hours from empty to full despite the extra motor output. The model also rides on 14-inch wheels. The Vietnamese prices start at VND 18.8 million (Rs. 68,400) for the Evo, VND 30 million (Rs. 1.09 lakh) for the Kyo and VND 40 million (Rs. 1.46 lakh) for the Kinet. The locally built scooters will compete in segments occupied by the TVS iQube, Bajaj Chetak Ather Rizta and Ola S1 series.
